use: a mechanism, one link at a time
request: Make a short explaining how car brakes actually stop the wheel. I always wondered what happens between my foot and the wheel.
topic: How a car's disc brake stops a wheel
intent: A curious driver wants the chain of cause from the pedal to the wheel.
goal: The viewer can trace the push from the pedal to the pads, link by link, and knows where the motion goes.
promise: A small push of the foot stops a heavy car, and you will see each link that carries it.
arc: Pedal and wheel far apart, then the links appear one at a time in causal order, ending on a hot disc.

events.text: Your foot pushes the brake pedal maybe five centimeters. So how does that stop a two ton car?
events.job: Open the gap between a tiny push and a heavy car.
events.knows: The push is small and the car is heavy.
events.waiting: What carries the push to the wheel?
events.look: the pedal, small, and the car's wheel far from it

events.text: The pedal pushes a piston into a cylinder full of brake fluid. Fluid can't be squeezed, so the pressure travels down the lines to every wheel.
events.job: First links: pedal to piston, piston to fluid, fluid pressure along the lines.
events.knows: Pressure in the fluid carries the push to every wheel.
events.waiting: What does the pressure do at the wheel?
events.look: the piston entering the fluid, then the pressure moving along the line

holds.does: the pressure arrives at the wheel end of the line, where the caliper waits

demo.what: the push traveling from the pedal through the fluid to the wheel

phases.why: one link at a time, in the order the push travels

events.text: At the wheel, that pressure pushes the caliper's pistons, which squeeze two pads against a spinning metal disc.
events.job: Last links: caliper pistons push the pads onto the disc.
events.knows: The pads clamp the disc from both sides.
events.waiting: Where does the car's motion go?
events.look: the two pads closing on the spinning disc from both sides

events.text: Friction turns the car's motion into heat. That's why the discs can glow after a hard stop.
events.job: Close the chain: motion becomes heat.

reveal.what: the disc heating as the car's motion becomes heat

quiz.q: In what order does the push travel from the foot to the wheel?
quiz.a: Pedal, piston in a cylinder of brake fluid, pressure through the lines, the caliper's pistons, the pads squeezing the disc.

quiz.q: Why can the brake fluid pass the push along?
quiz.a: Because fluid can't be squeezed (compressed), so the pressure travels through it.

quiz.q: What do the pads press against?
quiz.a: A spinning metal disc at the wheel.

quiz.q: How were the pads placed around the disc when they squeezed it?
quiz.a: One on each side of the disc, clamping it from both sides.

quiz.q: Where does the car's motion go when it stops?
In the opening picture, is the wheel near the pedal or far from it?
When the pressure reached the wheel end of the line, what was waiting there?
Which part of the wheel brake is shown turning hot at the end?
